bullets: Game 5 of 6 of a single-deck X-Bow session (video 754.2s-1051.0s); lost on the overtime lowest-tower tiebreaker to Graveyard Poison with double Goblin Hut, Ice Golem and Furnace — "we took a million more damage on the left. I thought we lost by 10 HP on the right. Okay, whatever. GG's, bro" (1042-1047s).

The X-Bow goes down early and often — [15, 11] right at clock 2:34, then [2, 13]/[2, 12]/[4, 12] on the left, two tiles off the river, from clock 1:31 onward — always with a bridge Berserker in front of it (t=824, 905, 980, 1007) rather than bare.

Berserker fills the mini-tank slot the knowledge-base list gives to the Knight, and this game points at the Hero variant: "Let's Berserker here at the bridge. Okay, we have an ability ready, but I don't think we're going to get the chance to pop it" (826-828s).

Evo Tesla is played 'high', 1-2 tiles from the river ([9, 14], [6, 13], [12, 13]), as an X-Bow bodyguard rather than a 3-tiles-from-bridge pull — "Evo Tesla is going to be really really important defensively. Let's just cycle a high Tesla now" (840-846s).

Against spawners the Fireball is spent on the building plus the tower on purpose: "whenever they go for this, they're just kind of just inviting you to Fireball their tower... I will eventually be up in damage" (795-803s); enemy left 4858 -> 4527 at t=798.

Defence is four 1-2 elixir cards in sequence — Electro Spirit, Skeletons, The Log, Berserker plus a Tesla — with Skeletons doing three distinct jobs: distraction ("Skeletons up top here to make sure that we distract this", 870s), blocking the enemy tower troop (881-883s), and going inside a Graveyard (970-971s).

Weakness exposed: a well-placed Goblin Hut plus a cycled Ice Golem shuts the win condition off completely. Twelve X-Bow deploy labels across 5 minutes produced one tick in regular time and one connection at overtime 0:05 — "Dude, is it even possible to connect with Expo in this match up? Like He has so many defensive options" (953-956s) and "I can't believe that it actually blocks an Expo" (898-901s).

new_deck.rationale: The X-Bow is the win condition and every other card is a 1-4 elixir defensive or cycle piece at 2.9 average elixir.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The X-Bow outranges the Crown Towers, so the deck's whole job is buying it the 3.5 seconds it needs and then keeping it alive; here that means a bridge Berserker in front of it on every siege (t=824, 905, 980, 1007) and an Evo Tesla cycled 1-2 tiles from the river as a bodyguard rather than as a standard pull building ("Evo Tesla is going to be really really important defensively", 840-846s). Swapping the Knight for the 2-elixir Berserker drops the average cost to 2.9 and gives the mini-tank a Hero ability, but it also gives up the Knight's bulk in front of the building. Fireball is the value engine against defensive buildings and spawners — Ryley takes the hut-plus-tower trade on principle ("they're just kind of just inviting you to Fireball their tower... I will eventually be up in damage", 795-803s) — while Electro Spirit, Skeletons and The Log handle everything cheap enough to leave the 6-elixir building affordable. The exposure this match shows is the classic siege one: a spawner placed where it physically blocks the X-Bow's line, plus a recycled Ice Golem, can hold the win condition off for a whole game ("I can't believe that it actually blocks an Expo", 898-901s).
